title: Om Prakash Puri v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam & Ors.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: V.K. Shukla, J.; Mahesh Chandra Tripathi, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; consumer relegated to statutory remedies under the Act and Supply Code.
headnote: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill of Rs. 2,49,846 and a direction to issue a revised bill was dismissed. The Division Bench held that a factual billing dispute cannot be adjudicated under Article 226. The Electricity Act, 2003 and the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 being self-contained, the consumer was left to the statutory remedy under those enactments.
facts: Om Prakash Puri was granted a 2 KW domestic connection (Service Connection No. 240789) at House No. 17/124, Deputyganj, Bulandshahr, after applying in December 2004; supply was energized and a meter installed on 18.12.2004. In May 2016 he received a bill dated 6.5.2016 demanding Rs. 2,49,846. He approached the licensee to have the bill revised, then invoked Article 226 seeking quashing of that bill and a direction to issue a correct revised bill so that he could pay.

holding_units.holding: A factual dispute as to the correctness of an electricity bill cannot be adjudicated under Article 226. The Electricity Act, 2003 and the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 are self-contained; the consumer must pursue the statutory billing-objection remedy available under those enactments.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the electricity bill dated 6.5.2016 demanding Rs. 2,49,846
not_decided.note: Left to the statutory remedy under the Electricity Act, 2003 and the Supply Code, 2005
